entries.proposition: The central finding: four heterozygous missense CACNA1I variants (three de novo or unproven) in six individuals with neurodevelopmental disease, with seizures in four, all behaving as gain of function in cell-line electrophysiology (hyperpolarising shifts of activation and inactivation, slowed kinetics, window current increased), the effect strongest in I860N and weakest in I860M, which tracks the milder clinical course in the family carrying I860M.
entries.snippet: All four disease-associated Cav3.3 variants show substantial gain-of-function effects on the gating properties.

entries.proposition: A single-patient treatment observation: one patient (case 1, de novo I860N) was treated with the non-selective T-type blocker ethosuximide, with improved seizure control, mostly fewer myoclonic seizures. It is reported in one Discussion sentence with no dose, endpoint, seizure counts, concurrent medication or time course; the Results state the same patient had daily myoclonic seizures and rare convulsive seizures that 'did not respond to treatment'. This is an uncontrolled anecdote in a mechanism-matched (T-type gain-of-function) channelopathy, not an effect size, and it is the only human ethosuximide-in-a-T-type-gain-of-function datum in R2.
entries.snippet: As a case in point, targeted treatment of Patient 1 with the non-selective T-type channel blocker ethosuximide resulted in improved control of seizures, in particular in a reduction of myoclonic seizures.

entries.proposition: Mechanism claim as the authors frame it: two parallel mechanisms, calcium toxicity from increased resting and action-potential-driven calcium entry in neurons expressing the variants from early development, and altered firing mode in thalamic neurons; the authors write it is uncertain how much developmental versus acute excitability changes contribute to network hyperexcitability and seizures, and they do not exclude a glial contribution.
entries.snippet: At present it remains uncertain to what extent deficiencies in early neuronal development and acutely altered excitability contribute to hyper-excitability on the network level and consequently to seizures.

entries.proposition: In a computer model of reticular-thalamic neurons, all four variants lowered the current needed to start firing and lengthened bursts beyond the stimulus, strongest for I860N. This is a simulation with parameters set from HEK-cell recordings, not recordings from neurons.
entries.snippet: Together, the data from the computer simulations of TRN neurons indicate that the altered gating properties of the Cav3.3 mutants cause a neuronal gain-of-function effect with severe hyper-excitability.
entries.anchor: Results, The mutant Cav3.3 channels increase neuronal firing in a model of thalamic neurons

entries.proposition: Phenotype breadth: of six patients, seizures were described in four, controlled on medication in two (cases 5 and 6, onset at 2 weeks and 2 years), refractory in case 1, late-onset in case 2; severe developmental delay, hypotonia, cortical visual impairment and feeding difficulties dominate. The syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder with seizures as one feature.
entries.snippet: Seizures began at age 2 weeks in Patient 5 and at 2 years in Patient 6 and are controlled on medication.
entries.anchor: Results, Heterozygous missense variants in the CACNA1I gene cause a spectrum of neurological symptoms
